newsitem.title: MEXICO: Legal row with NBC clouds Azteca's IPO.
newsitem.headline: Legal row with NBC clouds Azteca's IPO.

text.p: U.S. television network National Broadcasting Co has raised the stakes in its legal brawl with Mexican broadcaster TV Azteca -- a move which could give Azteca's upcoming initial public offering a black eye.

The companies traded barbs after NBC, a unit of General Electric Co, said it planned to seek at least $132.5 million in damages from Azteca for allegedly failing to live up to a 1994 deal that gave NBC the rights to 21.5 percent of Azteca.
"We have a very solid case and we believe the court will restore our rights ... (to a total) 21.5 percent of Azteca," NBC spokesman George Jamison said in a telephone interview late on Wednesday.
Mexico's number two broadcaster fired back by accusing NBC of trying to damage Azteca's reputation because the U.S. network felt its court efforts would fall short.

"It is clear to TV Azteca that NBC is not confident of its ability to win in the arbitration process and therefore is trying to damage the reputation of TV Azteca and affect its IPO through rumor and innuendo," Azteca said in a statement.

The dispute will not undermine what is expected to be a successful move by Azteca to offer some 22 percent of its capital on the New York and Mexican bourses -- the largest Mexican IPO since the 1994-95 peso crisis. The offer is due to be priced on Thursday and begin trading on Friday.

But it could cast a cloud over the issue by creating uncertainty about whether or not Azteca will have to issue new shares to NBC in the future, diluting existing shares, or pay out a hefty sum of damages.
"It is a serious concern, especially after the IPO price range was raised. It makes it a little less attractive," said a Mexico City analyst who asked not to be identified.

On Wednesday underwriter Bear Stearns Cos Inc said it had bumped up the price range on the IPO to $17-$19 per American Depository Share from $15-$17. Analysts said some investors were angered by the price hike and had decided to pull out of the offer.
"The offer still has very good demand, but less so than a few days ago," another Mexico City analyst said.

NBC earlier this week won a U.S. court order to subpoena five brokerage firms including Bear Stears for information about Azteca's IPO. NBC claimed it was misled by Azteca about the value of the company and its intentions to go public.

The move intensified a legal battle which began in April, when both firms took their dispute to the International Chamber of Commerce in Paris. The chamber is expected to take months to reach a verdict.
In the original deal, NBC agreed to license shows to Azteca, to allow the Mexican firm to use the NBC logo and to provide a host of consulting services.

In return, Azteca promised to pay $7 million in cash and granted NBC warrants to buy up to 10 percent of the broacaster for $160 million before May 1997. Azteca blocked the move in late April, sparking the legal battle.

The original deal also gave NBC rights to an additional 10 percent at market price when the company went public. In addition, NBC gained the right to 1.5 percent of Azteca's equity based on performance targets which were later met.
NBC says Azteca still owes it $5.2 million of the original $7 million.

NBC also wants Azteca to pay the difference between the strike price of the warrants and the likely market price of 10 percent of Azteca after the IPO. NBC says the difference will be worth at least $90 million based on a predicted total market capitalization for Azteca of $2.5 billion.
Finally, NBC says 1.5 percent of Azteca's equity would likely be worth another $37.5 million, bringing the total NBC wants from Azteca to at least $132.5 million.
